summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and alcohol dependence was admitted for nausea, vomiting, throat pain, and abdominal discomfort following a heavy alcohol binge shortly after a recent hospital discharge. He was diagnosed with alcoholic gastritis and mild pulmonary edema, with no evidence of acute cardiac ischemia, pancreatitis, or intra-abdominal pathology on imaging. He was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics, acid-suppression therapy, and symptomatic relief for throat discomfort, and gradually advanced to a regular diet. His kidney function and electrolyte abnormalities improved with supportive care. Alcohol withdrawal was managed with thiamine and diazepam as needed, and he remained stable. He expressed interest in future alcohol treatment but declined immediate transfer, opting to stay with his sister post-discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged and all home medications restarted.
